steps.title: Choose another Linux package
steps.instruction: Portcove manages the official x86-64 tarball. For Linux ARM64, use the official ARM64 tarball and open Snap64Recomp from the extracted folder. On x86-64 you can instead install the official .flatpak bundle and start io.github.jackandbeans.Snap64Recomp. Both tarballs need glibc 2.38 or newer, SDL2, GTK 3 and a Vulkan 1.2 driver.

steps.title: Set up the Android beta
steps.instruction: Install the official APK on ARM64 with Android 10 or newer and a Vulkan 1.2 driver. Android may ask your browser or file manager to allow app installation. For Internal storage > Snap64, allow storage permission on Android 10 or All files access on Android 11 and newer. Not now uses the app’s own folder and asks again on the next start. Don’t ask again keeps using the app’s own folder. Select your original in the app’s file picker.

steps.title: Supply your original
steps.instruction: Choose your own matching unmodified USA Pokémon Snap cartridge dump. Keep the original separately from each app’s imported copy.

warnings: Portcove manages the official Windows, Linux x86-64 and universal Mac packages. The Linux ARM64 and Flatpak packages and the Android APK use upstream or player-managed setup, replacement and data backups.
The Mac app needs macOS 14 or newer and is unsigned. If macOS refuses its first launch, follow the upstream instructions in its START HERE.txt (Open Anyway in Privacy & Security).
Upstream reports that its Mac app has run on GitHub-hosted Macs but not yet on physical ones; Portcove has no native Mac execution result for it.

references.title: Keep an upstream-managed profile
references.instruction: If you already use an upstream-managed copy, back up your actual Linux game folder or ~/.config/Snap64Recomp, the Flatpak folder ~/.var/app/io.github.jackandbeans.Snap64Recomp, or the Mac folder ~/Library/Application Support/Snap64 Recomp before replacement. Portcove-managed installs keep their data in the Portcove-managed profile and do not adopt these folders.

references.title: Keep the Android game folder
references.instruction: Back up Internal storage > Snap64 if you use the shared folder. If you use the app’s own folder, keep an accessible backup before uninstalling or clearing app data. To move to the shared folder later, enable All files access or the storage permission for Snap64 Recomp, then open the game. It copies missing game files and keeps existing files in Snap64. Check the shared saves before clearing the private folder. Install updates over the copy signed by the same upstream key.

references.title: Set up the game on Steam Deck
references.instruction: Use the official Linux x64 tarball or Flatpak and follow the project’s Steam Deck guide to add it from Desktop Mode. The publisher tested both 1.1.8 packages on a Steam Deck OLED in Desktop Mode. Earlier builds with the 1.1.7 Deck fixes also ran in Gaming Mode, where gyro aim sometimes felt slow. Follow the guide’s controller settings for the gyro mode you choose.

linux-x86-64: The managed Linux package needs glibc 2.38 or newer, SDL2, GTK 3 and a Vulkan 1.2 driver.
macos-x86-64: The unsigned Mac app needs macOS 14 or newer. If macOS refuses its first launch, follow the upstream instructions in START HERE.txt.
Upstream reports testing on GitHub-hosted Macs only. Portcove has no native Mac execution result for this app.
macos-aarch64: The unsigned Mac app needs macOS 14 or newer. If macOS refuses its first launch, follow the upstream instructions in START HERE.txt.
Upstream reports testing on GitHub-hosted Macs only. Portcove has no native Mac execution result for this app.

steps.title: Install with Portcove
steps.instruction: Choose your own unmodified USA Pokémon Snap cartridge dump. Portcove checks the original and installs the managed package for this device. Select Play when setup is complete.
